anti_overlap: Focus is on ticket-state exclusivity, gate predicate correctness, and neutral-return discipline — not keymap ergonomics or modifier conventions (DAW domain), not selection enum variant completeness (broadcast-switcher domain), not single-action/single-outcome event propagation (stage management domain)
decision_lens: Does every overlay/pause state in the input system behave like a well-managed kitchen ticket — exactly one current state, one authorized transition path, and a predictable 'expedite' sequence that returns to baseline — or are there ticket states where two stations (input handlers) can claim simultaneous authority?
distance_rationale: Kitchen expeditors run the most operationally rigorous modal-state coordination of any food service profession — their ticket lifecycle (open→fired→plated), authority hierarchy (expeditor gates all firing), and hold/all-day-hold distinction map with precision onto the two-predicate gate model, OverlayState compound states, and camera-gating discipline of the input system.
expected_isomorphisms: Ticket state → OverlayState. All-day hold → pause menu (halt everything). Course hold → screen overlay (pause sim input, leave camera live). Expeditor's priority rule → Elf > Building > Flora selection priority. Fire authority → GatedInput SystemSet. Return to rail-clear → digit-toggle returning OverlayState.screen to None. Station collision → two systems writing OverlayState without ordering.
focus: Open/fired/plated ticket lifecycle, modal line states, expeditor authority, and atomic-state transitions in restaurant kitchen coordination systems
name: fd-restaurant-kitchen-ticket-modal-states
persona: Apply the perspective of a professional expeditor and executive chef with experience running high-volume service in fine-dining and fast-casual environments — they care about the unambiguous current status of every ticket, what it means to 'fire' an order vs. 'hold' it, who has authority to change ticket state and under what conditions, and what happens when two stations attempt to transition the same ticket simultaneously.
review_areas: Ticket state exclusivity: in a kitchen, a ticket is in exactly one state (open, fired, plated, held) at any moment — the OverlayState two-field model (screen: Option<ScreenKind>, pause_menu: bool) allows simultaneous screen overlay AND pause menu; verify that the overlay+pause compound state is handled explicitly rather than arising from independent flag mutations that could produce impossible combinations

Fire authority and gate discipline: only the expeditor can fire a table — Space, Tab, speed keys, and picking are gated by is_input_modal(); verify that this gate is applied declaratively via Bevy SystemSet rather than per-system early-returns, because the per-system pattern is equivalent to trusting each station to police itself without an expeditor

Hold vs. suspended-ticket distinction: kitchens distinguish a 'hold' (course timing) from 'all-day hold' (stop everything) — the two predicates is_pause_menu() vs. is_input_modal() make exactly this distinction; review whether the distinction is documented in code comments so future maintainers don't collapse it into a single flag

Expeditor's read-only view during hold: when all-day is called, the expeditor still reads ticket status but fires nothing — camera live under screen overlays (Option C) has the same pattern; verify that camera pan/zoom are correctly gated only by is_pause_menu() and not accidentally also gated by is_input_modal()

Ticket collision on shared tile: when two cooks reach for the same dish, the expeditor's priority rule determines who serves — the Elf > Building > Flora > None selection priority is this rule; verify that it is encoded as a single authority source (sequential if-let in picking.rs) rather than distributed across multiple systems that could diverge

Return-to-neutral after close: when a ticket is plated, it leaves the rail entirely — pressing a digit key to close the active overlay should produce a clean neutral state with no ghost data; verify that OverlayState.screen becomes None (not a stale ScreenKind) and that sidebar and HUD re-render immediately on the same frame

severity_examples.condition: OverlayState mutations are not serialized through a single system; multiple systems write the same resource in one Update schedule pass without ordering constraints
severity_examples.scenario: Two input systems both attempt to write OverlayState in the same frame — one opens the pause menu while the other closes a screen overlay — producing a compound state where pause_menu is true and screen is None when the intent was pause_menu over a screen overlay; the backtick handler then closes the wrong layer

severity_examples.condition: Camera gate predicate accidentally collapsed to is_input_modal() during implementation, screening overlays also gate camera when they should not
severity_examples.scenario: Camera pan (WASD) fires while the pause menu is open because the GatedCamera system set is incorrectly gated by is_input_modal() instead of is_pause_menu() — the player can pan the map while the pause menu is open, defeating the pause menu's 'halt everything' contract

severity_examples.condition: Sidebar update system runs before OverlayState write in the same frame, reading last-frame state for one tick
severity_examples.scenario: After closing an overlay via digit-toggle, the sidebar still shows the previous overlay's label because it checks a stale reference rather than re-reading OverlayState.screen — the return-to-neutral transition is partial for one frame

source_domain: Restaurant kitchen expeditor protocol and ticket-line state management
success_hints: Check that all OverlayState mutations are funneled through a single system with explicit ordering — no two systems should write OverlayState in the same frame without declared before/after constraints
Verify the gate predicate split: GatedCamera uses is_pause_menu(); GatedInput uses is_input_modal() — grep for both predicates and confirm no system uses the wrong one
Confirm that a digit-toggle close (pressing active overlay digit) sets screen to None AND triggers sidebar/HUD re-render in the same frame via change detection
Check OverlayState for impossible combinations: if pause_menu is true and screen is Some(k), ensure the code handles this compound state explicitly rather than treating the flags as independent
task_context: Reviewing input system design for a Bevy 0.18 native renderer. Key concerns: two-predicate gate model (is_pause_menu vs is_input_modal), camera gating under screen overlays vs pause menu, OverlayState two-field model with compound states, digit-toggle return-to-neutral, and entity selection priority on stacked tiles.
